intent: Split three near-miss linux_configuration scripts under the cap, and confirm the shell-split pattern holds on a small batch before scaling it.
scope: Non-goal: no script executed, no behaviour change
changes: Moved the idle-inhibit process and controller watchers, the mtkclient udev/venv setup, and the Gitea firewall/UPnP/router block into sourced libs, each following the pattern from the install_joplin.sh commit: shebang, chmod +x, no set -euo pipefail, and SCRIPT_DIR via ${BASH_SOURCE[0]}.
mtk_root/install.sh already declared SCRIPT_DIR readonly, so the split reuses it rather than redeclaring; its existing $0 was upgraded to ${BASH_SOURCE[0]} at the same time.

Fixed two shellcheck findings the split exposed. persist_with_systemd_logind now takes the persist flag as an argument instead of reading the caller's global, so the lib is checkable standalone. python_bin in the mtkclient setup was assigned and never read - dead code, deleted rather than carried into the new file.
Neither finding was introduced by the split: shellcheck already reported three SC2034 warnings on the pre-split mtk_root/install.sh.

verification.command: scratchpad/verify_split.sh <script> <moved functions> -- bash -n, shellcheck -x, then a stubbed run
verification.evidence: All four scripts (including install_joplin.sh from the previous commit) now report 'libs sourced, functions defined'. The stubbed run found a real bug static checks missed: mtk_root/install.sh aborted with 'SCRIPT_DIR: readonly variable' because the splitter inserted a second declaration. bash -n and shellcheck were both clean on that broken file.
SC2154 on persist_systemd and SC2034 on python_bin, both fixed at the source rather than suppressed. Clean afterwards.

verification.command: systemctl cat dns-blocklist-refresh media-organizer, then test -f the ExecStart path
verification.evidence: Both resolve to existing files. Neither script was touched in this batch, but the check is cheap and these are the only two units pointing into the repo.

verification.command: pre-commit run --files <changed>, then the real git commit for jscpd
verification.evidence: Clean. jscpd stayed under 2% with three new libs added at once, which is what the small first batch was sizing up - the libs carry no set -euo pipefail or source-guard boilerplate, which is what would have driven duplication.
Entry scripts 180, 141, 198; libs all under the cap.

risks: None of these scripts was run. turn_off_auto_idle_screen_shutdown.sh drives idle inhibition and logind, mtk_root/install.sh installs udev rules and a venv, and setup_gitea.sh opens a firewall port - all excluded by decision 6. The stubbed run proves the libs are reachable and the functions defined; it does not prove the scripts still do their job.
persist_with_systemd_logind's signature changed. Its only caller was updated in the same commit, and grep confirms there is no other.

The verifier mirrors the repo tree into a temp dir so repo-relative sources like ../../lib/common.sh resolve. A script sourcing something outside linux_configuration/scripts would not be covered by that mirror.
rollback: git revert the commit; the three scripts return to 289, 262 and 255 lines and the three libs disappear.
After rollback, re-run bash -n and shellcheck on the restored scripts.
